title: Security Review - Data Residency & Region Pinning
summary: Redwood and FinBridge reviewed region pinning and data residency requirements for a EU-sensitive workload. Covered SOC 2/ISO posture, SSO/RBAC, audit logs, KMS integration, sub-processor list, and possible architecture options (hosted region pinning vs Dedicated/Private). Agreed next steps: send SOC2/ISO docs, DPA, region pinning guide, and schedule a technical runbook + pilot in EU region.
next_steps: Redwood to share SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 summary and DPA (Aisha) - due 2026-03-24
Provide list of subprocessors and data flow diagram (Marco) - due 2026-03-25
Schedule Private/Dedicated architecture walkthrough and pilot plan (Sofia/Aisha) - schedule by 2026-03-28
FinBridge to send security questionnaire and legal contact for DPA (Liam) - due 2026-03-23
action_items: Aisha: Send SOC2 report and ISO summary via secure link - 2026-03-24
Marco: Export current subprocessors list + brief on cross-border subprocessors - 2026-03-25
Sofia: Prepare region-pinning runbook (hosted vs dedicated vs private) and short cost delta - 2026-03-28
Hannah: Provide example workload topology and latency SLOs we need for pilot - 2026-03-24
Liam: Return executed DPA draft or redlines - 2026-03-30
transcript:
[00:00] Aisha (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining. we, um, are here to go through the security and residency requirements for the new FinBridge EU workload. I think Jonah wanted to lead with the primary constraint?
[00:12] Jonah (FinBridge): yeah thanks, aisha. short version - our company needs strong assurances that customer data for EU customers stays in the EU and never gets processed in the US, except where explicitly permitted. also auditability: SOC 2 type II and ISO references, SSO, audit logs, and KMS integration.
[00:26] Aisha: great, thanks. Marco and Sofia from our infra and se team are on to cover the how - region pinning, private options, and subprocessors.
[00:35] Marco (Redwood SE): hi everyone, quick intro. our platform supports region pinning for hosted endpoints - you can pin an org or a model route to eu-west-1 and we will route inference to capacity in that region. we also have Dedicated pools and Private (VPC/on-prem) which give stronger guarantees if you need zero-data-exit assurance.
[00:55] Priya (FinBridge Security): when you say "route to eu-west-1", is there any possibility of control-plane metadata or logs ever leaving the region? we have to prove no cross-border transfer for eu-personal data.
[01:06] Marco: good q. control plane metadata is limited; our hosted control plane is multi-region but we provide options. for stricter customers we can do a private control plane deployed in their VPC (that stays in region), or we can provide region pinning plus contractual commitments and subprocessors that are EU-based. i'll pull up the subprocessors doc in a sec.
[01:22] Hannah (FinBridge): also, what about backups and snapshots - are they geo-replicated by default? that's a red flag for us.
[01:28] Sofia (Redwood SE): backups for hosted by default are encrypted and may be replicated for durability; for EU-only residency we recommend either Dedicated with EU-only storage or Private deployment where snapshot replication policy is in your control. we can also disable cross-region replication for pinned routes.
[01:44] Jonah: and encryption at rest - we need to use our KMS key, not yours.
[01:48] Marco: we support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations (bring-your-own-key). on AWS we can use your AWS KMS in the same account when using Private or Dedicated; for hosted we offer a BYOK flow with a dedicated keystore and HSM-backed wrapping. there are some operational details - key rotation, rekeying during migrations - we'll document.
[02:05] Priya: good. audit logs - can we get immutable audit trails for data access, model invocation, and admin actions? retention for at least 12 months, exportable?
[02:15] Sofia: yes, we expose audit logs with detailed event types: invocation, admin, config, auth events. logs can be forwarded to your SIEM (e.g., Splunk, Datadog) or pushed to an S3 bucket you control in the EU. retention policies are configurable; default 90 days, but enterprise plans can extend.
[02:33] Jonah: what about SOC 2 and ISO certs, and the scope - does it include private deployments or only hosted?
[02:40] Aisha: our SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 cover the Redwood control plane and hosted services; for Private deployments the customer controls the environment but we provide documentation and hardening checklists. we'll share the SOC2 report and ISO summary.
[02:53] Liam (FinBridge Legal): i need to see subprocessors list and DPA terms that include region pinning guarantees and breach notification SLAs.
[02:59] Marco: sure - subprocessors list is in our compliance pack. note that some third-party infra or telemetry systems may be outside EU; we'll flag those and propose EU-only equivalents where possible.
[03:13] Priya: about cross-border processing - what's Redwood's policy if a model training or fine-tuning job touches EU data and backend tooling is in the US?
[03:21] Marco: we separate training pipelines; Redwood's hosted inference does not train on customer inference payloads by default. for any fine-tuning you'd opt into that and we'd need a written agreement and controls. training infra may live in the US for certain models; for customers requiring EU-only processing you'd use Private or Dedicated in EU where training or any storage would remain in EU.
[03:41] Hannah: can you also confirm whether any telemetry or performance metrics include PII? we scrub payloads, right?
[03:48] Sofia: yes we have payload minimization; telemetry is aggregated and PII is redacted. still, we can route telemetry to your EU SIEM to avoid sending anything elsewhere.
[03:58] Jonah: what about subcontractors for content moderation or human review? do you use human-in-the-loop anywhere?
[04:05] Marco: we generally do not have human review of inference payloads. any human review that occurs for abuse or safety would be explicit and noted in subprocessors; for enterprise customers we can disable any human-review flows.
[04:16] Priya: ok, good. can you walk through the concrete options and tradeoffs - hosted region pinning vs Dedicated vs Private?
[04:23] Sofia: sure - hosted region pinning: easiest to start; we route inference to EU GPUs and store EU-only snapshots when configured, but control plane metadata might still be in a global control plane unless you opt into our private control plane add-on. tradeoff: lower operational overhead, less absolute guarantee.
[04:39] Sofia: Dedicated: reserved capacity in EU-only clusters, customer tenancy for inference capacity, stronger isolation, and can be configured to use your KMS. tradeoff: higher cost (commitment) but simpler compliance posture.
[04:51] Sofia: Private (VPC/on-prem): full control - private control plane in your VPC, no cross-border control plane, can use your networking and KMS. tradeoff: most operational responsibility and a longer onboarding timeline.
[05:03] Jonah: are there any known cross-border subprocessors we can't avoid in hosted?
[05:08] Marco: a small set of telemetry and analytics providers historically are US-based; we have EU alternatives but there may be migration effort. we'll include exact names in the subprocessors doc.
[05:16] Liam: on legal guarantees, we need region pinning contractual language in the DPA - not just "best efforts".
[05:23] Aisha: absolutely. for customers signing up for EU pinning we can include contractual commitments and audit rights; for higher risk customers we recommend Dedicated or Private plus contractual language. we'll have legal draft language for the DPA.
[05:36] Priya: any SLA for accidental cross-border transfer or mis-routing events? aside from remediation, we need notification windows and indemnity?
[05:45] Aisha: standard incident response is 24 hours initial notification; for enterprise we can negotiate faster windows and specific remedies. indemnity will be handled in the master services agreement and DPA negotiation.
[05:56] Hannah: latency is a concern - if we pin to eu-west-1, what are typical p95 latencies for the families we've used?
[06:02] Marco: depends on model size; for small-medium models p95 is sub-200ms from eu-west-1 to EU-region frontends; for large models it can be 400-800ms. Dedicated can reduce variance since you control pool sizing. we'll share benchmark spreadsheets.
[06:17] Jonah: curious about logging architecture: where are audit logs stored and who has retention control?
[06:22] Sofia: logs can be pushed to your EU S3, or kept in Redwood log storage with configurable retention. access is RBAC-controlled, and logs are immutable with append-only write path; exportable as needed.
[06:35] Priya: SSO and RBAC - we want SAML SSO + SCIM and fine-grained roles. does Redwood support that?
[06:42] Aisha: yes, SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning supported. RBAC supports role templates and custom roles; we can map roles to SCIM groups. we also have admin audit trails.
[06:52] Hannah: for KMS integration, is there a recommended flow for minimal trust - e.g., envelope encryption where Redwood never holds plaintext keys?
[06:59] Marco: we use envelope encryption patterns. with BYOK you control the key material; Redwood gets wrapped keys but not plaintext. for Private deployments you can operate keys wholly inside your VPC and HSM.
[07:12] Jonah: will you run a pilot with eu-only pinning? what does onboarding look like?
[07:17] Sofia: pilot approach: 1) scoping call (this week), 2) exchange minimal config (IAM/KMS/region), 3) deploy region-pinned endpoint in eu-west-1, 4) run test workloads and capture logs/metrics. pilot typically 2-4 weeks.
[07:30] Priya: we want proof that control-plane ops won't leak metadata. can you provide architecture diagrams?
[07:35] Marco: yes - we'll provide a data flow diagram and a control-plane separation doc.
[07:39] Aisha: quick recap before we end: we'll send the SOC2 & ISO summary, subprocessors list, DPA draft, region pinning runbook, and propose pilot dates. any other asks?
[07:50] Liam: please include explicit DPA language for region pinning guarantees and breach notification timelines.
[07:55] Hannah: include example commands for forwarding audit logs to our EU S3 and steps to configure BYOK.
[08:02] Jonah: thanks all. we'll review documents and revert with a pilot window by end of week.
[08:07] Aisha: thanks everyone. follow-ups in the next couple days. bye.

Notes on transcription: occasional overlap and filler. names sometimes abbreviated (Aisha/Ash). timestamps approximate. "eu-west-1" shorthand for EU region. Some product names truncated (KV cache -> kvcache), minor mis-hearings around specific legal phrasing.
